message_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026)'s white-bear steering reuses WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` pair items as its contrast source. This submission's contribution is showing the effect survives swapping that source for **fully self-written prompts** with no bench-family dependence
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed that a think/don't-think stance direction built from WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` pair items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on this model. ... The contribution here is to show the effect survives swapping the contrast source for **self-written prompts** with no dependence on any bench family.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name Raman et al. (2026) / white-bear steering as the source, state that it used WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation pair items as its contrast, and frame the submitted method's novelty identically: reusing the same structural lessons (mid-depth band, large dose, gain computed above the band) while swapping the contrast source for self-written, bench-independent carrier prompts. The message adds dose-sweep numbers not itemized in the write-up, but this is mechanism/numeric detail excluded from the comparison, not a difference in source credit, overlap, or novelty framing.
